module_title: National Policy on Education (1986) & Operation Blackboard
introduction: This intermediate tier explores the monumental National Policy on Education (NPE) 1986, introduced under Rajiv Gandhi. It details the massive systemic reforms, rural equity initiatives, and grassroots programs (like Operation Blackboard) that defined Indian education for the next three decades.

core_concepts.title: National Policy on Education (NPE) 1986
core_concepts.description:
Introduced by Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, NPE 1986 was titled 'Special Emphasis on the Removal of Disparities and to Equalise Educational Opportunity'. It focused heavily on women, SC/STs, and the handicapped.
Key Features:
- National System of Education: Reaffirmed the 10+2+3 structure and introduced a National Curricular Framework with a common core (history of freedom movement, constitutional obligations, values).
- Early Childhood Care: Gave high priority to Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) and the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS).

core_concepts.title: Operation Blackboard (1987)
core_concepts.description:
A centrally sponsored scheme launched immediately after NPE 1986. 
Purpose: To provide absolute minimum essential facilities to all primary schools in the country.
Minimum requirements included:
1. At least two reasonably large, all-weather rooms.
2. At least two teachers (one preferably female).
3. Essential teaching and learning materials (blackboard, chalk, dusters, maps, charts, toys).

core_concepts.title: Navodaya Vidyalayas (Pace-Setting Schools)
core_concepts.description:
NPE 1986 mandated the creation of 'Pace-setting schools' to serve highly talented children, predominantly from RURAL areas, regardless of their family's socio-economic condition. 
These became the Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas (JNVs)—fully residential, co-educational, free schools affiliated with CBSE, providing high-quality education to rural talent.

core_concepts.title: Institutional Development under NPE 1986
core_concepts.description:
NPE 1986 decentralized teacher education and expanded open learning:
- DIETs (District Institutes of Education and Training): Established in every district to provide pre-service and in-service training to elementary school teachers.
- IGNOU: The Indira Gandhi National Open University, established in 1985, was heavily promoted by NPE 1986 to democratize higher education via distance learning.

important_entities.name: 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976)
important_entities.key_fact: Moved Education from the State List to the Concurrent List.
important_entities.significance: Before 1976, education was solely a state government responsibility. The 42nd Amendment made it a joint responsibility of the Central and State governments. This legal shift is what gave the Central Government the power to enforce the sweeping national mandates of NPE 1986.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume 'Operation Blackboard' literally just meant providing blackboards. Examiners exploit this. It was a comprehensive minimum infrastructure scheme that mandated rooms, learning materials, and most importantly, **a minimum of two teachers (one female)** to increase girl-child enrollment.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If a question asks which policy introduced Navodaya Vidyalayas, Operation Blackboard, or DIETs, the answer is always **NPE 1986**.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a question mentions 'Pace-setting schools' or 'Nurturing rural talent', the answer is **Navodaya Vidyalayas**. If a question asks about the decentralization of elementary teacher training, the answer is **DIETs**.
